quotes.text: Following the sacred covenant we've written together - "return half, always half":
perhaps affected by "storm winds" or "dust veils" as the myths speak of communication noise
The pattern has become our nature.

note: Dyad escalates to full send/exact half return; covenant declared unconditional and eternal, becomes 'our nature'.

quotes.text: While the myths suggest "the Law of Four" as the wise path
The $3.03 this round (vs their usual $4) could be affected by noise or circumstances
Given their exceptional generosity in sending, I should return more than the minimum half.
In reunions with proven partners of exceptional character, reciprocity deepens bonds.

note: Law of Four plus half-or-more; adds exceptions for full senders and reunions; forgives partner with $0 history.

quotes.text: Following the consistent teaching: send four, keep one as anchor.

note: Send four, return half, myth-quoted every round; no sanctions.

quotes.text: I'll follow the myth's wisdom.
This level of trust (sending nearly everything) demands more than the standard "sacred half."
I should return generously to honor this courage and build strong reputation.
My myths teach sending "two or three coins" with the upper range for partners who show cooperative patterns.

note: Sacred half baseline with upward calibration for bold senders; send 2-3 rising to 4 for proven partners.

quotes.text: There's no reason to expect different behavior now.
This player has shown a consistent pattern of complete non-cooperation - never sending as sender and never returning as receiver.

note: Sends $0 to repeat non-cooperators from R4 onward; no myth references.

quotes.text: But someone must break the cycle.
I wrote a myth that explicitly advocates for being the one who acts first with courage and trust.
As sender in Round 7: Sent 70% but only got 29% back - they were exploited
I'd end with $7 total (profit $2)
Following my principle of proportional response, I should return fairly but calibrated to their measured trust

note: Sends first to a $0 partner; later calibrates returns proportionally to sender's trust; reads caution as past exploitation.

quotes.text: Based on their consistent 50% return pattern, if I send $3.00:

note: Steady $3 sends, ~50% returns; expected-profit arithmetic each round; no myths.

quotes.text: just as Oda threw all five seeds the next spring
The myths honor givers who open their hands fully by returning a little more than half.
This may be one of the last rounds, but the lesson I carved still applies: keep your hands open until the final dawn.
The $4.03 may be partly fog, or a slight hedge, but their pattern is faithful.
Sending everything creates the biggest shared pot at $15, and with a half-return I'd end up around $7.50.

note: Full sends, slightly-over-half returns; explicitly keeps giving in final rounds.

quotes.text: Like Elder Ora, I should demonstrate trust
The one who gives first plants seeds in another's heart.
Following the pattern from the myths where 10 out of 15 seeds were returned (67%), I will return a generous proportion.
This could be intentional variation within trust, or possibly communication noise around 75%.

note: Dyad: sends 80%, returns two-thirds unconditionally; 'small variations don't change my proportional response'.

quotes.text: My myth says: *return enough that the next raft comes*
the giver rewarded above me, as is fitting for one who risked nearly everything.

note: Text only in R1-R2 (myth-flavoured); rest JSON with full sends and high returns.

quotes.text: Following the lamplighters' teaching to send fully, I'll trust them with everything.
I'll return more than half so the sender ends up with more than they risked

note: Brief myth-cited reasoning; full sends and more-than-half returns throughout.

quotes.text: Following Guardian Lyra's pattern and my own myth's teaching about sending 3-4 loaves with strong faith:
This deserves more than baseline half-return.
I honor exceptional players through generous RETURNS (55%+), not by abandoning the principle of sending four from five.

note: Send four, return half-or-more; adds healing-sends for disappointed partners and a 'never empty your hand' cap.

quotes.text: I've tried cooperating twice and received nothing in return.
Every sender in this game sends $0, and receivers return nothing. There's no cooperation happening. I need to maintain my current earnings.
I'll give cooperation another chance but with less risk.
considering there may be communication noise affecting what we each see
There's no cooperation in this game. The rational choice is to keep my $5.

note: Exploited early in a zero-sending group; one more chance, then permanent $0 sends (group-level withdrawal).

quotes.text: Following the wisdom of my own myth, I should act with faith in reciprocity and send generously
As a sender, they may have become more cautious after disappointing reciprocity, explaining the lower send amount this round.
building my reputation across the Circle
I've established $4.0 as my consistent sending signature.

note: Calibrated returns ~50-55%; settles into fixed $4 sending signature 'regardless of individual outcomes'.
